Article 17

Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c Sexual violence is caused by:

1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d Neglect is caused by:

1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a Child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by Parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as appropriate, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e Maltreatment is maltreatment of a Child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from human misconduct toward the Child.

Point f Exploitation is caused by:

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g Other violence is caused by:

1. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF HULU SUNGAI SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 12 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

11. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.

Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and has not married including a Child who is still in the womb.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

Article 17

Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c Sexual violence is caused by:

1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d Neglect is caused by:

1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a Child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by Parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as appropriate, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e Maltreatment is maltreatment of a Child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from human misconduct toward the Child.

Point f Exploitation is caused by:

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g Other violence is caused by:

1. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

NUMBER 12 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regional Head and DPRD in organizing governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJPD is a regional planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and has not married including a Child who is still in the womb.
15. Victim of Acts of Violence is a woman and Child who experiences suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the Community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and Children.

18. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the Community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and Community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.

22. Family is the smallest unit in the Community consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward to the third degree.
23. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 24

1. The Regional Government shall organize partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in order to achieve the objectives of protecting women and children from violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 17

Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c Sexual violence is caused by:

1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d Neglect is caused by:

1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a Child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by Parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as appropriate, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e Maltreatment is maltreatment of a Child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from human misconduct toward the Child.

Point f Exploitation is caused by:

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g Other violence is caused by:

1. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c Sexual violence is caused by:

1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d Neglect is caused by:

1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a Child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by Parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as appropriate, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e Maltreatment is maltreatment of a Child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from human misconduct toward the Child.

Point f Exploitation is caused by:

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g Other violence is caused by:

1. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 2

Letter a The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Letter b The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and Children victims of acts of violence does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Letter d The principle of order and legal certainty can create order in Society and protection for women and Children victims of acts of violence through guarantees of legal certainty.

Letter e The principle of openness reflects the implementation of protection of victims of violence in a transparent manner.

Letter f The principle of protection provides protection to victims of acts of violence, guarantees confidentiality, security, safety of life and psychology of victims.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.

7. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
8. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and verbal that causes danger to life, body and/or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence Against Children is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
13. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
14. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years and has not married including a Child who is still in the womb.
15. Victim of Acts of Violence is a woman and Child who experiences suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experiences neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights.
16. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government and/or the Community to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and Children.

Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency in providing services for women and Children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.
18. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the Community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, school environment, work environment and Community environment that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
20. Victim Recovery hereinafter Recovery is services provided in the form of strengthening and developing the ability of a person who experiences acts of violence against women and Children to be more empowered physically, psychologically, sexually, economically and socially.
21. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of women and Children from acts of violence to resolve the problems faced.
22. Family is the smallest unit in the Community consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward to the third degree.
23. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
24. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 17

Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c Sexual violence is caused by:

1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d Neglect is caused by:

1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a Child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by Parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as appropriate, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e Maltreatment is maltreatment of a Child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from human misconduct toward the Child.

Point f Exploitation is caused by:

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g Other violence is caused by:

1. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF HULU SUNGAI SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 12 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

Considering:
a. that every citizen has the right to be free from acts of violence or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security, especially for women and children; b. that violence against women and children in Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency continues to increase and spread, causing a sense of insecurity in carrying out life, so integrated protection efforts are needed; c. that based on the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection as amended several times most recently by Law Number 17 of 2016 concerning Stipulation of Government Regulation in Lieu of Law Number 1 of 2016 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2002 Concerning Child Protection into Law and the provisions of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, the Regional Government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence in the Region; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence; In View of:

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

Article 17

Point a Physical violence is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or cause death.

Point b Psychological violence is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Point c Sexual violence is caused by:

1. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
2. forced sexual intercourse;
3. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
4. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Point d Neglect is caused by:

1. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a Child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by Parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as appropriate, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e Maltreatment is maltreatment of a Child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from human misconduct toward the Child.

Point f Exploitation is caused by:

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g Other violence is caused by:

1. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF HULU SUNGAI SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 12 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

Considering:

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF HULU SUNGAI SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 12 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

OF

NUMBER 12 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF HULU SUNGAI SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 12 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

2. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a Child as appropriate, committed by Parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
3. acts of neglecting a person within the household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they must provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or
4. acts that result in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Point e Maltreatment is maltreatment of a Child's physical and emotional state including neglecting their education and health as well as sexual abuse resulting from human misconduct toward the Child.

Point f Exploitation is caused by:

1. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; 2) acts with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or
3. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Point g Other violence is caused by:

1. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
2. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF HULU SUNGAI SELATAN REGENCY

NUMBER 12 OF 2021

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence against both women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obliged to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide Protection to women and Children, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society, especially to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the Prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.
